messages.subject: POFIND
parts:
When I use "pofind", I get this error: " condition not found in the data".
Automatically the error appears to me even when I search for complex, intermediate and parsimonious solutions. How can I do?

messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: Re: [QCA] POFIND
parts:
Dear Chiara,

I can see the screenshot, but it doesn't help me very much. I need to replicate your problem in order to trace the source of the error.
Could you perhaps prepare a so-called MRE - minimal reproducible example?
That includes either your actual data, or some R commands that would create a test data for which the pofind() command fails. Either option you choose, the ideal is to send the smallest possible subset of your data or the smallest possible test data for which the error can be replicated.

Best wishes,
Adrian

The script misses the command to import your data, which should be:
fuzzy_data <- read.csv("fuzzy_data.csv", sep = ";", row.names = 1, dec = ",")

But even so, I cannot replicate your error, as I get:

class(fuzzy_data)

After that, I suggest you might try to re-import your own data (using my above command) and re-run the pofind() function? If working as above, this must have something to do with your current object containing the data.

Additionally, as per the welcome message of this forum, users should report the version of the QCA package along with their operating system, by pasting the results of these two commands:
